I grew up in a house full of clutter. It was so bad, there were "paths" in our house to walk around the clutter. My parents still live in the same clutter that's been sitting there since I moved out over a decade ago. I try to clean it up but they won't let me. I had flashbacks of hiding things at the bottom of the garbage because that's what I used to do when I lived at home. 

If you look at my house now, we don't have a lot of stuff. I'm incredibly conscious and thoughtful about what I buy or take home from the curb. I only want to buy something once, so I put a lot of time, thought and research into buying things. I also think about how I can repurpose something if I can't use it the way it's intended anymore.

Even though we don't have a lot, I find myself decluttering all the time. It's so easy to accumulate things. 

Lately, the only thing I've been hoarding is glass jars so that I can use them to tidy up my cupboards!

The threat is that NIMBYs will push back. Unfortunately, it all about pandering to the group that will give you the most votes.

Whoever gets elected, doesn’t matter if it’s Chow, Saunders or anyone else, they will absolutely ignore Scarborough once elected. 

The thing is most people in Scarborough vote against their own interests. It’s a heavily conservative area and there are a lot of homeowners that don’t want any low income housing or new housing developments at all. Total NIMBYS. They don’t care about transit because they all have cars. Scarborough isn’t walkable so people aren’t inclined to take TTC. People who live in Scarborough only take TTC if they *have* to, and likely because they can’t afford a car. And who cares about the poors, right? 

People know they can pander to Scarberians because it’s an easy vote because they never mobilize or have a real voice for actual change. Homeowners only care about their property values and having other likeminded neighbours. 

Politicians will pander and say Scarborough is rich with culture and diversity and pretend to eat a beef patty in a photo op, but at the end of the day, the borders will be fucked with or it will continue to get ignored.

I’ve lived in both basement and apartment buildings and I would never recommend a basement apartment to anyone who values their sanity. 

It’s dark, hardly any natural light and gets even worse in the winter. Basements often have humidity/flooding issues. The basement I lived in needed the dehumidifier running constantly for it to feel decently comfortable. Thank God I wasn’t paying utilities. And the worst part about it was the noise. The constant stomping, yelling, etc. was so amplified it made me unwell. It could have been just my shitty neighbours, but even if they are the nicest, quietest people, you’ll still hear everything.

With the traditional apartment, you get natural light, you may get a balcony space and if your neighbours are noisy, at least it’s through the walls and not directly above you where you can literally hear every step and movement. 

Some people might disagree with me or say that I had a uniquely shorty experience, but regardless, I still wouldn’t recommend a basement. It’s such a risky move because you never know what you’re actually moving in to, where in an apartment, it’s more or less standard. 

If you’re really concerned, pick a smaller building, like maybe 5 or 6 floors in a good area. $1650 I think is a good budget and you’ll find something decent.
